transcript:
Meeting: Onboarding governance, technical & cost breakout
Date/Time: 2025-03-27 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Lucas Rivera (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood CSM); Sara Patel (AlderTech Procurement), Danilo Ruiz (AlderTech Infosec), Karen Wu (AlderTech Platform), Mark Fletcher (AlderTech Legal)

Summary: quick alignment on MSA/DPA expectations, KMS/SSO precheck, cost model for pilot (dedicated vs hosted), and next steps for legal redlines and pilot SOW. Some transcription noise around K V cache and quantization terminology; agreed to share benchmarks and security pack.

Topics: MSA redlines; DPA data residency and audit rights; SLA tiers and uptime definitions; SSO/SAML and SCIM; KMS/HSM and keying options; pilot scope and pricing; egress/bandwidth/hot-cache cost concerns; dedicated capacity vs hosted with private tenancy.

Action items (brief): see metadata for owners/due dates.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about an hour, big thanks to Sara and team for coordinating. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Lucas our SE will walk through the technical cost bits. Priya's here for pilot ops.
[00:18] Sara Patel: Hi, thanks. Just to flag procurement is here to get the MSA sign pathway and any major exceptions up front. We need to know what are the must-haves vs negotiable items.
[00:26] Maya Chen: Totally. We want a pragmatic path to pilot while limiting long legal cycles. We'll share redlines we typically accept and call out items that need escalation.
[00:35] Danilo Ruiz: From infosec, quick things: SSO (SAML), SCIM for provisioning, audit logs, and KMS — we want customer managed keys ideally. Also curious on SOC2 scope and ISO 27001 if you have it.
[00:47] Lucas Rivera: Yep. We support SAML SSO, SCIM, and key wrapping via AWS KMS or custom HSM partners. For private deployments we offered-- we, uh, Redwood Private gives you the option to bring your KMS or we can integrate with your HSM, that path is common. Our SOC2 Type II report's in the security pack.
[01:05] Mark Fletcher: Legal — our focus is audit rights, data residency, incident notification windows, and indemnity carveouts. Also escrow for models but that's lower priority for the pilot.
[01:17] Maya Chen: Understood. For the pilot we usually accept a narrow audit window and standard incident timelines; we'll flag any nonstandard indemnity asks.
[01:27] Karen Wu: Technical question — can you confirm what stays in our VPC versus what stays on Redwood control plane? We need clarity for data flow and egress costs.
[01:36] Lucas Rivera: Great question. For Redwood Private, control plane metadata (like routing) still is light, but inference nodes and model weights can be deployed inside the customer VPC. So token payloads can stay in your VPC and K V cache is local — sorry, I mean KV cache. The big egress is model updates if you choose cloud hosted model catalog. If you pin a model in private, there shouldn't be steady egress.
[01:58] Sara Patel: When you say model weights in VPC, do you mean we need dedicated GPU hosts? What's the price delta versus hosted API?
[02:06] Lucas Rivera: Yes, dedicated capacity uses reserved GPU pools. For rough ballpark, dedicated lowers per-token cost for steady high throughput. For a small pilot (low qps) hosted can be cheaper upfront. We'll run numbers.
[02:17] Maya Chen: We're going to share a pricing workbook. It will show example workloads: interactive chat, batch embeddings, and reranker flows — and compare dedicated vs hosted with burst capacity.
[02:26] Danilo Ruiz: Also want to understand key lifecycle: can Redwood access plaintext keys? We need proof that keys are never exported and that customer controls rotation.
[02:35] Lucas Rivera: We have two modes: customer-managed KMS (recommended) where keys never leave your KMS; or Redwood-managed with envelope encryption. For customer-managed KMS, we only receive ciphertext and perform operations without key export. We'll put the whitepaper excerpt in the security pack.
[02:47] Mark Fletcher: On DPA and data residency — AlderTech processes EU customer PII, so we need EU processing only for certain datasets. Is region pinning available?
[02:57] Maya Chen: Yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated and Private. Hosted customers can pick region, but we should confirm data boundary guarantees; Lucas will note specifics for the security doc.
[03:09] Karen Wu: Curious about SLA. What percent uptime do you guarantee for Dedicated vs Hosted? And what are remedies?
[03:16] Lucas Rivera: Dedicated has SLA tiers — typically 99.9% with availability credits. Hosted is operationally very reliable but SLA depends on plan. We'll attach the SLA appendix. Remedies are credits, not termination for pilot agreements normally.
[03:31] Sara Patel: Procurement question — what approvals do we need for pricing? We usually do a three-month pilot followed by procurement assessment. Are month-to-month or committed discounts available?
[03:40] Priya Singh: We can offer a pilot pricing model: a time-boxed pilot with a baseline committed min and overage. For committed reserved capacity we do a discounted commit monthly or annual. We'll include pricing bands in the SOW.
[03:52] Danilo Ruiz: About egress fees — can you quantify typical network egress? We have strict budgets for bandwidth.
[03:59] Lucas Rivera: Egress depends on token volume and if you stream. Typical chat payloads are small; embeddings output can be larger. We'll provide a cost-per-GB example and show how KV caching reduces repeated prefix costs.
[04:12] Maya Chen: Note — caching reduces calls to the model for repeated queries, so for workflows with repetitious context it lowers cost significantly.
[04:19] Karen Wu: You mentioned quantization and model variants earlier. If we use quantized variants to save cost, is there a quality regression risk we need to document?
[04:27] Lucas Rivera: There can be small diff in outputs; Redwood Optimize provides quality regression monitoring and we recommend baseline evals against a golden prompt set. We'll include a suggested eval plan.
[04:38] Mark Fletcher: Legal — we'd like to see sample redlines to the MSA to speed review. Also define what ‘‘confidential information’’ includes — platform telemetry? Logs?
[04:47] Maya Chen: We'll send a redline template and call out items that typically require enterprise addendum. Telemetry can be scoped; we usually agree logs are operational but PII is excluded unless it's needed for support.
[04:56] Sara Patel: Timeline — if we get redlines within a week and agree pilot SOW, can we start in mid-April? Our procurement committee meets next week.
[05:05] Priya Singh: That's feasible; timeline looks like redlines this week, SOW by Apr 7, kickoff Apr 14, pilot run two to four weeks.
[05:14] Lucas Rivera: Quick technical note — for the pilot we'll recommend spinning up a small dedicated pool if your expected qps is >200, otherwise hosted with burst and a pinned region is simpler. We'll include cost thresholds.
[05:26] Danilo Ruiz: One more on keys — the DPA needs to explicitly state retention windows and right to delete; we will want a 30-day deletion confirmation SLA for test data.
[05:35] Maya Chen: We can include deletion confirmation within 30 days for pilot. For production, retention windows are negotiated.
[05:42] Mark Fletcher: Also need export control language and whether cryptography controls need to be stated.
[05:47] Lucas Rivera: We'll surface the cryptography controls in the security pack and link to the compliance matrix.
[05:53] Sara Patel: Pricing approvals - will you accept a PO with final SOW and a short-term MSA? We sometimes need a PO to release pilot funds.
[06:01] Maya Chen: Yes we accept PO for pilot. We'll include billing contacts in SOW.
[06:07] Karen Wu: Ops question — how will we onboard teams for keys and SSO? Do you provide runbooks?
[06:14] Priya Singh: We have onboarding runbooks, SSO guides, and step-by-step KMS integration docs. Lucas will link the runbooks in follow-up.
[06:22] Lucas Rivera: I'll upload a quick-start repo and a kube/helm example for Private deployments — note some of the commands are slightly different per cloud.
[06:30] Speaker 1: (crosstalk) Sorry, I just want to confirm the benchmark we want: latency p95 under 500ms for chat is our target.
[06:37] Lucas Rivera: For chat p95 < 500ms is doable with tuned batch sizes and local KV cache. We'll run baseline numbers against your example payloads.
[06:45] Sara Patel: Procurement — what support SLAs come with pilot? We may want a named CSM.
[06:50] Priya Singh: Pilots include CSM support hours and an SE ridealong for deployment. Named CSMs are part of enterprise packages; for pilots we can assign a primary CSM.
[07:00] Maya Chen: Quick recap — action list we'll follow: send MSA/DPA redlines and security pack, Lucas to run and share benchmarks/cost workbook, Priya to draft SOW. Redwood to accept PO for pilot.
[07:12] Mark Fletcher: Sounds good. Anything else on the technical gating?
[07:17] Karen Wu: Single signoff item — SCIM provisioning must be supported for our Okta flows.
[07:21] Lucas Rivera: SCIM supported and we've got sample manifests for Okta.
[07:25] Danilo Ruiz: Also pen test window — we want to run a light pen test on the integration before production.
[07:30] Maya Chen: We'll align on pen test dates and scope; we'll coordinate with infosec.
[07:34] Sara Patel: Ok last procurement note — if legal redlines are minor we can sign MSA and start pilot; if there are major changes we escalate to our CPO.
[07:43] Maya Chen: Understood. We'll aim to minimize major exceptions.
[07:47] Priya Singh: I'll propose dates for the SOW and kickoff in follow-up, and add meeting invites for the legal review.
[07:55] Speaker 2 (Karen Wu): Quick nit — do you charge for data egress during model snapshot restores? Because we snapshot models to update weights and that could spike egress.
[08:03] Lucas Rivera: Snapshot restores do have a one-time transfer cost if you're pulling weights across regions; we'll highlight scenarios and mitigations (model pinning, local caching).
[08:13] Maya Chen: Great. If there are no more questions we'll close and send notes. Thanks everyone.
[08:18] Sara Patel: Thanks all, we'll expect the redline set and pricing workbook.
[08:21] Mark Fletcher: Thanks, speak soon.

[Redwood follow-up links promised during call]
- Security pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS outline) - to be attached in follow-up email
- Pricing workbook / benchmark CSV - Lucas will upload and share link
- MSA redline template - Maya will attach
- SOW skeleton - Priya will attach

End of transcript.
